A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the models developed for ILATPS have good performance, but the use of more complex models can improve the accuracy of the predictions.

, for the first time, the analysis of the accuracy and extrapolation ability of the most common models to describe the binodal curve in ILATPS has allowed the development of a new equation with a reduced number of adjustable parameters and a better accuracy.

the use of an empirical equation with just one additional adjustable parameter is enough to obtain a high accuracy in the description of the binodal curves of ionic liquid-based aqueous two phase systems, and the proposed equation could be used to model any ILATPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the binodal curve modeling of ionic liquid–salt aqueous systems is not a trivial task, and the selection of an appropriate model is crucial to obtain accurate and precise phase diagrams, especially when extrapolation is needed or when the model is used in other thermodynamic properties.
the choice of a model to describe the binodal curve is not trivial, as it depends not only on the accuracy of the model but also on the type of information needed for the system studied.

, when the accuracy is important, the use of a simple explicit equation is recommended to describe the binodal curve in the whole range of the concentrations of ionic liquid, and the model developed in this study can be a good choice.
